Reads and edits GanttProject files (.gan) on Android.

Files are edited in place: settings, calendars, baselines and anything else this app does not know about are preserved untouched, so a project can move between phone and desktop freely.

Free software under the GNU GPL v3.
Changes are saved automatically when you leave the app or close the project.
The planned duration of %1$d working days does not match this effort. At the current assignment it would be %2$d days.
Assign a resource to see how many days this effort corresponds to.
Read-only — reopen it with “Open project” to be able to save
This file has changed since you opened it — the desktop saved it, or your cloud folder brought down a newer copy. Saving now would erase that work.
Tasks that are running or start soon — tick them off and record time.
Tap to open the app and choose a project for this widget.
The project could not be read. Tap to open the app.
Nothing on this phone writes to the project file.
Edit here, where you can see the project and are asked before anything gets overwritten.
In the app and the widget
Also allows ticking tasks off and recording time straight from the home screen.
Editing is switched off for this device. You can turn it back on under Settings.

This project is a file in a synced folder. Nothing decides which of two competing changes is the real one: if you edit here and the desktop saves before the sync has caught up, your change is gone without a trace.

The app refuses to overwrite a file that changed since you opened it — but it cannot bring back a change that was overwritten somewhere else.

At risk are progress, the completed mark and hours you typed in by hand. Hours from the time tracker are safe: what was imported is recorded in the project file, so a lost change simply means those entries are offered again next time.

Enter a project folder, not the collection root — the root often allows browsing but refuses saving. Projects on a WebDAV server are version-checked on save. Without a server the app keeps using files from your device.
Connected. The server supports locking, so a project open on the PC cannot be overwritten from here.
Connected, but the server does not support locking. Conflicts will be detected on save, not prevented.
The address must start with https://. The password is sent with every request.
Signed in, but not allowed to use this folder.
No such folder on the server.
Someone has this project open on the PC. Your changes are safe and stay on the phone. Saving works again once it is closed there, at the latest after two hours.
The server did not report a version for this project, so it cannot be saved safely. Reopen it and try again.
The server could not be reached (%1$s).
No projects found on the server.
You are signed in, but this folder is not shared with your account. Open a project from a folder you have access to, or ask for it to be shared.
This project is no longer on the server. It may have been renamed or deleted.
The server address in the settings is not a valid address. Check that it holds only the address, for example https://example.com/projects/.
Open on the PC right now
This project is open on the PC right now. You can read and edit it here — saving will be refused until it is closed there, at the latest after two hours.
